title: Identifying Food Labeling Effects on Consumer Behavior
eligible_reason: Main reduced-form specifications (Tables 2-4, columns 2 and 5; Table 6) regress daily store-SKU outcomes on a binary warning-label indicator with store-SKU fixed effects and calendar-time (week-of-year plus day-of-week) fixed effects, no controls, two-way clustering by store and SKU. Labels switch on at store-SKU-specific dates (50-55 distinct first-label dates per category among switchers) and never-labeled SKUs provide an untreated comparison group, so the design is staggered binary adoption. Caveat: label is not absorbing (roughly 45% of switching store-SKUs show label=0 after first labeling); per PROTOCOL Section 5b, post-adoption periods with label=0 must be dropped. Always-treated store-SKUs (labeled from the first visit day, May 2, 2016) are present.
design_notes: Store-SKU-day panel of three snack categories (cereals, chocolates, cookies) in 6 stores of a Chilean supermarket chain, 56 visit days from 2016-05-02 to 2016-07-22 (a_week 18-29). Data products.dta: 50,496 rows, 3,698 store-SKU groups (957 cereals, 1,076 chocolates, 1,665 cookies). Per category: never-labeled groups 467/380/534; always-labeled 162/299/334; switchers 328/397/797 of which 145/223/446 are non-monotone (label turns off after first appearance). Distinct first-label dates among switchers: 50/55/55 (daily). Time FE are a_week (week of year) and dow (day of week), both deterministic functions of the calendar date; Table A2 uses date FE instead. Treatment timing test (Table 7) regresses days-to-labeling on 2015 sales, quantity and price to argue timing is not driven by product characteristics. Structural (demand) part is separate (R/Apollo) and not relevant.
n_adoption_cohorts: 50-55 distinct daily first-label dates per category (switchers); plus always-labeled and never-labeled store-SKUs
n_adoption_cohorts_note: Counted from Data products.dta: first date with label==1 within group_store_sku, by category.

specs.treatment_definition: label = 1 if SKU j in store s carries at least one front-of-package warning label on visit day t (0/1); labels appear at store-SKU-specific dates during the May-July 2016 roll-out of the Chilean labeling law (effective June 27, 2016); not an absorbing state (old and new packaging coexist, so label switches on and off within some store-SKUs)
specs.time_var: date (daily store visits; FE at a_week + dow level)
specs.fe: group_store_sku (store x SKU) + a_week (week of year 2016) + dow (day of week)

data_provenance: real (SKU identifiers masked, prices shifted by a constant; quantities and transaction counts as collected). Structural-analysis CSVs are described as disguised but are not used here.
data_files: Data households cereal/choc/cookies.dta (+ placebo versions, 57-363 MB)
software_notes: Stata reghdfe/esttab/boottest; code shipped as a .docx file (Code product and household.docx). Structural part in R.
screener_notes: Screened from package only (no article text). Main-text table numbering inferred from code comments ('Tables 2, 3 and 4: Main effects' looping over cereals, chocolates, cookies; 'Table 6: Effect on price'); verify against the published PDF. The absorbing-state violation is substantial: replication must define adoption as the first labeled date and drop later label=0 rows (Hull footnote 6), which removes many treated observations. CSA requires a single time index: use date (daily) with store-SKU as the unit; the TWFE uses week + day-of-week FE, so an exact FE match in CSA/BJS is not possible, note the deviation. Package dir: ~/did_packages/mksc/mksc.2022.1356; regressions_path list is empty because the code is stored in a .docx.
